data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts that the single cross-city modulator is city size because 'a larger contiguous area of impervious surfaces generates a deeper and more persistent volume of warm air.' This mechanism is physically unsound: the nocturnal UHI is governed by the local energy balance at each point (stored heat release per unit area, reduced longwave radiative loss via restricted sky view, anthropogenic heat). Total city area does not increase the per-unit-area heat release, and atmospheric advection on a clear calm night is minimal. The well-established dominant cross-city modulator in the urban climatology literature is the sky view factor (street canyon geometry), which directly controls longwave radiative cooling efficiency — not total impervious extent. The 'deeper volume of warm air' argument conflates a plume/dispersion concept with the surface energy balance that actually drives the nocturnal UHI.
